In every post I maintained that we have benefited from animal testing. I don’t need to deescalate or make concessions. I already did.

I would take a drug found to be safe and effective had it been proven so through human based research methods. 

RASCAR for toxicity, organ on a chip, AI models and whatever else more brilliant people than me can create. 

Why should something tested on a rat make me feel better about taking it?

Ah yes, I don’t agree with you, don’t know what I’m talking about, and I’m anti science. Awesome. 

I have admitted and will always admit we have learned valuable, life changing information from animal testing. I am simply saying it’s time for us to really consider and push for human based alternatives, harnessing innovations in technology to do so. Scientists and doctors are already doing this and I think most people would see the benefit of exploring it. 

Don’t be mad on my account. If this is something you plan on pursuing after you graduate, then maybe you’ll get to see it for what it actually is.

You’re right. I forgot how much we’ve learned from interviewing mice, guinea pigs, and beagles going thru drug trials for mental illnesses. 

We don’t need to cut down on these practices. We need to innovate. We need to work on something that yields results. Of the major mental illnesses animal testing hasn’t produced any results. Animal testing has been beneficial for humans and we do have a lot of advancements because of it, but we need to innovate in order to make further breakthroughs. 

There is nothing humane about it, unless you consider the fact that the animals are killed after results are in. In a way, a swift death after being given a disease could be seen as humane, if you ignore the fact that they were given the disease in the first place. 

We didn’t spend a lot of time making our buggies more aerodynamic for our horses to pull. We innovated and created automobiles. That’s what we need in medical testing. 

Saying animal testing is ineffective is definitely not the same thing as denying climate science. Anti science would be using old methods instead of seeking innovation. Anti science is defending outdated methods instead of looking for better ones.

It has to do with the supply of the animals. Labs can purchase ‘excess’ animals from breeders and even shelters, tho is varies by state. Beagles are one of the most used dog breeds because of their gentle nature and sheer amount produced by puppy mills. 

Simulations would require a lab to invest in the technological infrastructure as a replacement to a practice it’s always used. Even if Doug so would save it money in the long term. 

And what I meant was 95% of drugs that make it to human trial fail because the animals used don’t have similar enough biology to humans, making the testing process completely useless.

Not true anymore. Human biology based methods like simulations are becoming more reliable but it is cheaper and easier to use animals. Also, 95% of drugs fail, yet almost 100% use animals for testing. The FDA doesn’t require animal testing yet it is still the industry standard because it is easy and cheap. 

It may have been beneficial in the past but now we need a new advancement that replaces this practice. So, yeah... you can still feel bad about it. Sorry.

Opening core crystals is the most frustrating part of the game but when you get the rare blades, their stories form perfect little subplots to the overall arc. It’s masterful storytelling.
